topic_brief.title: Organic vs conventional farming crop yield gap
topic_brief.research_question: How much lower is crop yield under organic farming compared to conventional farming?
topic_brief.intervention_description: Organic farming system (certified organic or following organic principles: no synthetic fertilizers, no synthetic pesticides)
topic_brief.comparator_description: Conventional farming system (using synthetic fertilizers and/or pesticides)
topic_brief.outcome_description: Crop yield (grain, fruit, or total biomass harvested per unit area)
important_moderators: Crop type (cereal, legume, fruit, vegetable, oilseed, root/tuber)
Crop species (wheat, maize, rice, soybean, tomato, potato, etc.)
Experiment type (long-term trial, on-farm comparison, field trial)
topic_brief.benchmark_source: Ponisio et al. 2015 (Proc R Soc B 282:20141396)

rows.title: Comparative economic analysis of crop yield under organic and conventional farming systems in Punjab, Pakistan
rows.treatment_description: Organic farming (natural manure, minimal pesticides)
rows.control_description: Conventional farming (NPK fertilizers, synthetic pesticides)
rows.notes: Survey of 300 farmers (153 organic, 147 conventional) in 2019. Parenthetical values in Table 4 interpreted as SE based on large sample sizes (SE with n~90 gives realistic CV~15%). Mean difference 853.67 kg/ha reported as significant (T=4.63 for within-organic district comparison, T=4.02 for within-conventional). Rabi season wheat.

rows.title: Comparative economic analysis of crop yield under organic and conventional farming systems in Punjab, Pakistan
rows.treatment_description: Organic farming (natural manure, minimal pesticides)
rows.control_description: Conventional farming (NPK fertilizers, synthetic pesticides)
rows.notes: Survey of 300 farmers in 2019. Jhang district. Parenthetical values interpreted as SE. Mean difference 458.26 kg/ha. Table 4 reports within-system district differences (566.03** and 613.66**) rather than organic-vs-conventional t-stats directly, but text states organic yield was significantly lower by 11% overall.

rows.title: Effect of organic farming on the restoration of soil quality, ecosystem services, and productivity in rice–wheat agro-ecosystems
rows.treatment_description: Organic crop management (FYM 7.84 t/ha, vermicompost 3.13 t/ha, neem cake 853 kg, Sesbania green manuring)
rows.control_description: Inorganic crop management (DAP, muriate of potash, urea; recommended NPK doses)
rows.notes: Organic rice yield significantly HIGHER than inorganic. Data averaged across 4 locations and 15 years (2004-05 to 2017-18). LSD is for crop management main effect comparison. n not explicitly stated; design has 3 reps at each of 4 locations = 12 plots per treatment per year, averaged over 15 years. Organic management included Sesbania green manuring which likely boosted rice yield.

rows.title: Analysis of farming systems establishes the low productivity of organic agriculture and inadequacy as a global option for food supply
rows.outcome: Human metabolizable energy (HME) - grain only, organic crop farms vs conventional crop farms
rows.treatment_description: Organic farming without livestock (OFC), Paris Region France, grain HME only. Derived: 0.39 x 85 = 33.15 GJ/ha/yr
rows.control_description: Conventional farming without livestock (CFC), Paris Region France, grain HME
rows.notes: COMMENTARY PAPER - no primary data. Treatment mean derived: paper reports OFC/CFC grain HME ratio = 0.39 and CFC = 85 GJ/ha/yr (stated in text). 56 OFC farms, 76 CFC farms. Rotations in OA typically 7-9 years with legume-based fodder; CA rotations short ~3 years.

moderators.mod_crop_type: mixed grain crops (cereals, oilseeds, grain legumes)

rows.title: Analysis of farming systems establishes the low productivity of organic agriculture and inadequacy as a global option for food supply
rows.outcome: Human metabolizable energy (HME) - grain only, organic mixed crop-livestock vs conventional crop farms
rows.treatment_description: Organic mixed crop-livestock farms (OMCL), Paris Region France, grain HME only. Derived: 0.27 x 85 = 22.95 GJ/ha/yr
rows.control_description: Conventional farming without livestock (CFC), Paris Region France, grain HME
rows.notes: COMMENTARY PAPER - no primary data. Treatment mean derived: paper reports OMCL/CFC grain HME ratio = 0.27 and CFC = 85 GJ/ha/yr. Only 14 OMCL farms vs 76 CFC farms. This ratio excludes milk production from OMCL livestock.

moderators.mod_crop_type: mixed grain crops (cereals, oilseeds, grain legumes)

rows.title: Analysis of farming systems establishes the low productivity of organic agriculture and inadequacy as a global option for food supply
rows.outcome: Human metabolizable energy (HME) - total food (grain + milk), organic mixed crop-livestock vs conventional crop farms
rows.treatment_description: Organic mixed crop-livestock farms (OMCL), Paris Region France, total food HME (grain + milk). Directly stated as 30 GJ/ha/yr
rows.control_description: Conventional farming without livestock (CFC), Paris Region France, total HME (grain only, as CFC has no livestock). Directly stated as 85 GJ/ha/yr
rows.notes: COMMENTARY PAPER - no primary data. Both means directly stated in text: 'a major difference in food production (HME) between the OA (30 GJ/ha/yr) and CA systems (85 GJ/ha/y)'. Ratio = 0.35. This is the most favorable OA comparison (includes milk from ruminant conversion of pasture). 14 OMCL vs 76 CFC farms.

moderators.mod_crop_species: mixed cereals, oilseeds, grain legumes + dairy cattle

rows.treatment_description: Organic farming, southernmost Swedish region (most productive), HME from milk + remaining grain
rows.control_description: Conventional farming, southernmost Swedish region, HME from milk + remaining grain
rows.notes: COMMENTARY PAPER - no primary data. Values from Swedish government statistics across 8 S-N regions. This is the southernmost (most productive) region endpoint. OA/CA ratio ~0.35. No per-region sample sizes given; total national areas: OA 331,970 ha, CA 1,724,790 ha.

rows.title: Analysis of farming systems establishes the low productivity of organic agriculture and inadequacy as a global option for food supply
rows.outcome: Wheat grain yield - organic after 3yr lucerne vs conventional regional average
rows.treatment_description: Organic wheat yield following 3 years of lucerne in a well-documented rotational experiment, Paris Basin
rows.control_description: Conventional wheat, regional average yield, Paris Basin
rows.notes: COMMENTARY PAPER - no primary data. OA wheat yield 3.2 t/ha described as 'closer to 1960 yields'. CA regional average 7 t/ha. No variance or n reported. The OA yield is after a record-breaking 3yr lucerne rotation (best-case BNF scenario), yet still far below CA. High CA wheat yields of 10 t/ha achievable in France/Germany with chemical fertilizer.

rows.title: Soil nitrate accumulation and leaching in conventional, optimized and organic cropping systems
rows.treatment_description: Organic alfalfa-winter wheat system (ORG); alfalfa grown this season; 74 kg N/ha from cattle manure; optimized irrigation 250 mm
rows.control_description: Conventional winter wheat-summer maize system (CON); wheat grown this season; 300 kg N/ha urea; 325 mm irrigation
rows.notes: ORG grew alfalfa this season while CON grew wheat. Yields converted to food equivalent units (FEU: wheat=0.991, alfalfa=0.7). Not a like-for-like crop comparison. Significance letters: CON/OMW/OFW=a, ORG=b.

rows.notes: ORG grew alfalfa while CON grew maize. Different crops compared via food equivalent units. Significance: CON/OMW/OFW=a, ORG=b.

rows.title: Soil nitrate accumulation and leaching in conventional, optimized and organic cropping systems
rows.treatment_description: Organic system (ORG); winter wheat; 197 kg N/ha from manure; 275 mm irrigation; rotary tillage
rows.control_description: Conventional system (CON); winter wheat; 300 kg N/ha urea; 450 mm irrigation; rotary tillage
rows.notes: SAME CROP comparison (both wheat). Most reliable observation for organic yield gap. Significance letters: OMW=a, OFW=ab, CON=b, ORG=c. Note CON=b meaning ORG significantly lower than CON.

rows.title: Soil nitrate accumulation and leaching in conventional, optimized and organic cropping systems

rows.notes: ORG grew alfalfa while CON grew maize. Significance: CON=a, OMW/OFW=b, ORG=c.

rows.title: Soil nitrate accumulation and leaching in conventional, optimized and organic cropping systems
rows.treatment_description: Organic alfalfa-winter wheat system (ORG); total 345 kg N/ha over 2 years from manure; 525 mm total irrigation; rotation: alfalfa-alfalfa-wheat-alfalfa
rows.control_description: Conventional wheat-maize system (CON); total 1200 kg N/ha urea over 2 years; 925 mm total irrigation; rotation: wheat-maize-wheat-maize
rows.notes: 2-year cumulative yield. Abstract reports 46% yield decline for organic. Different crop rotations compared (alfalfa-wheat vs wheat-maize) using food equivalent units (FEU: wheat=0.991, maize=1.001, alfalfa=0.7). Significance: CON/OMW/OFW=a, ORG=b. Source of variation: treatment***, season***, treatment×season***.
